data.title: 2.5 mn jobs, ₹5 meals, farm loan waiver: SP releases UP polls manifesto
data.description:
The Samajwadi Party on Thursday released its manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, promising 2.5 million government jobs over five years, a monthly unemployment allowance of ₹5,000 for graduates and an annual pension of ₹40,000 for elderly women.
 
Unveiled by party chief Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow on Constitution Day, the manifesto, titled 'Sattais Ka Sankalp: PDA Ka Pran Patra – Jan-Man Ka Manifesto 2027', places employment and welfare at the centre of the party's electoral promises. It also proposes a caste census, a legal guarantee for minimum support prices (MSP) for 23 crops and milk, an immediate farm-loan waiver and free electricity for rural households.
 
 

Akhilesh Yadav says 'bure din' are about to end

 
Taking aim at the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Yadav said the 'Acche Din' promised by the party had not arrived and that its time in power was nearing an end.
 
"We are releasing our manifesto today because 'acche din' never came, but 'bure din' are about to go away. They know that they are about to be ousted, so their language has changed," Yadav said at the launch.
 
He also accused certain powerful groups of trying to weaken the Constitution to protect their influence. "Our country will be governed by 'samvidhan' (Constitution) and not 'manvidhan' (arbitrariness)," he said.
 

2.5 mn government jobs, ₹5,000 monthly allowance for graduates

 
Employment is one of the key focus areas of the manifesto. The  Samajwadi Party has promised 2.5 million government jobs over five years and 20-30 million employment opportunities in other sectors during the same period.
 
Graduates who remain unemployed will receive a monthly allowance of ₹5,000 until they find work. The party has also promised an annual calendar of government vacancies and a transparent, time-bound recruitment process. Recruitment involving a single examination will be completed within three months, while processes involving multiple examinations will take up to six months.
 
The party has proposed skill training for 2 million young people every year, along with an Urban Employment Guarantee Act and residential hostels for male and female students in major cities. It has also promised opportunities for Agniveers who are not granted permanent commissions in the Army.
 

Education: 26,000 schools to reopen, laptops for students

 
The party has promised to reopen 26,000 primary schools that Yadav alleged were shut by the present government. It also plans to revive its free laptop-distribution scheme for students who pass Class 12.
 
A special State Education Policy will be introduced to ensure equal access to quality education, with particular attention to PDA communities and economically weaker sections. The party has proposed Wi-Fi facilities in primary and secondary schools and an allocation of 6 per cent of the state's gross state domestic product (GSDP) to education.
 
The manifesto also promises to regularise shiksha mitras, subject to legal advice, and increase their monthly honorarium by ₹5,000. The party has pledged action against examination paper leaks and greater accountability for officials and ministers.
 

Caste census, reservation and welfare measures

 
The manifesto proposes a caste census across Uttar Pradesh to identify the social and economic conditions of different communities and frame welfare policies accordingly.
 
The party has promised to allocate 20 per cent of the state Budget to the development of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (SC/ST). It has also proposed special recruitment drives to fill vacant reserved posts and a Dalit Startup Fund.
 
One of its key proposals is 50 per cent reservation for Dalits and PDA communities in government contracts worth up to ₹50 crore. A Dalit Development Council, chaired by the chief minister, is also proposed.
 
For economically weaker sections, the party has promised Samajwadi canteens serving meals at ₹5 per plate. Elderly women, including women artisans, will receive an annual pension of ₹40,000, transferred directly to their bank accounts. Labourers, women workers and artisans have also been included in the proposed annual pension scheme.
 

Farm loan waiver, legal MSP guarantee for 23 crops

 
The party has promised an immediate waiver of farm loans and a legal guarantee for MSP covering 23 crops and milk. It has also proposed compensation for farmers growing other notified crops.
 
A fund of ₹15,000 crore will be created to ensure timely payments to sugarcane farmers. The party has promised free electricity for agricultural irrigation and up to 300 units of free electricity for rural households.
 
It has also proposed an allocation of ₹1.5 trillion for rural infrastructure development.
 

Healthcare, law and order

 
The manifesto proposes a State Health Policy 2027, with a focus on affordable healthcare and medical education. Poor and PDA patients will receive free treatment at government hospitals, while families below the poverty line (BPL) will be provided health insurance cover of ₹10 lakh.
 
District hospitals will be equipped with intensive care units and ventilators, while super-speciality hospitals will be established in all 18 administrative divisions. The party has also promised to upgrade the cancer hospital in Lucknow into a leading facility in north India, with free cancer treatment.
 
On law and order, the party has promised action against caste- and religion-based violence, crimes against women, land-grabbing networks and organised crime. It has proposed a dedicated women's policing system, village-level safety arrangements and 33 per cent representation for women in new police recruitment.
 

MSMEs, traders and workers

 
The party has promised a new Industrial Policy 2027 to revive micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), along with time-bound clearances through a single-window system.
 
A Trade Security Commission and a special police force for traders have also been proposed. For workers, the party plans to introduce a Dial 1890 Mazdoor Power Line to address grievances, including those of Uttar Pradesh residents employed outside the state. A Migrant Labour Card scheme and equal pay for equal work are also part of the manifesto.
 
Elderly construction workers will receive an annual pension of ₹40,000 and health insurance cover of ₹10 lakh.
 

Infrastructure, urban development and other promises

 
The manifesto promises four-lane roads connecting all tehsil headquarters and paved roads in every village. It also proposes round-the-clock electricity across villages, towns and cities.
 
For urban areas, the party has promised round-the-clock water supply in cities with populations above 1 million, improved drainage systems to prevent flooding, better traffic management and new greenfield townships. Measures to reduce air pollution and restore the scheme for converting Nazul land into freehold property have also been proposed.
 
Other commitments include the restoration of the Old Pension Scheme for government employees, an end to outsourcing in government departments, a Public Service Delivery Act and technology-based measures to curb corruption.
 
The party has also promised to promote tourism, develop a Heritage Arc covering historically and culturally significant cities, establish three world-class stadiums and 10 sports colleges, and introduce welfare measures for journalists and lawyers.
 
The manifesto includes promises for minority welfare, including protection against hate crimes, better representation in higher education and support for artisans and weavers. For the armed forces, it proposes free education for children of martyrs and a pension scheme for their families, while reiterating its opposition to the Agniveer scheme.
 
(With agency inputs)

data.title: Nifty IT index flags breakout from 3 important chart patterns; details here
data.description:
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion. Brokerages PL Capital and Emkay in their technical reports on the Nifty IT highlighted that the index has broken out from three important chart patterns on the daily charts. The Nifty IT index has moved up 2.4 per cent to 33,387 thus far in November. However, it has rallied 20.5 per cent thus far in the last quarter of 2026, and up almost 30 per cent from its nadir this year. The IT index has witnessed a sharp reversal since July. Prior to this, the index was the top laggard this year, down nearly 29 per cent in the January - June period. Following the recovery, brokerages believe the Nifty IT index now looks favourably placed on the charts and could see a trend reversal here on. CHECK Stock Market LIVE Updates 

PL Capital flags breakout from 'Golden Cross' and 'Descending Trendline'

PL Capital in its technical report on the Nifty IT index said that it signalled a 'Golden Cross' and 'Trendline Breakout,' thus setting the start for a trend reversal. The term 'Golden Cross' means that the Nifty IT index 50-day moving average (50-DMA) has now crossed over the 200-DMA, signalling near-term strength. Further a descending trendline is formed joining the preceding highs (lower highs) on the charts. The Nifty IT has witnessed a strong recovery and is currently testing its long-term descending trendline resistance at 33,000–33,300, says PL Capital. "The formation of a Golden Cross, coupled with a rising RSI at 63.42 and early signs of improvement in Relative Strength (RS) against Nifty 50, indicates a strengthening technical structure," explains the brokerage. Analysts at PL Capital reckon that a decisive weekly close above the trendline, supported by higher volumes, could pave the way for a move towards 35,500 and subsequently 38,000–39,000, thus marking a potential reversal of the prolonged corrective phase for the IT index. The brokerage adds that the 30,100–30,600 zone remains a key support area. Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE 

Emkay flags breakout from an 'Inverted Head-and-Shoulders' pattern

 Technical analyst at Emkay note that the Nifty IT index has broken out of an inverted head-and-shoulders pattern. An 'Inverted head-and-shoulders' chart pattern is the opposite of 'head-and-shoulders' wherein the middle dip, out of three declines is deeper than the other two, followed by a breakout from the neckline joining the first and the last highs. "The Nifty IT index has witnessed an inverted head-and-shoulders pattern near the lower band of its five-year range, following a 40 per cent correction and a 40-week consolidation, indicating a potential trend reversal with an estimated 18 per cent upside to 39,000," says Emkay in its technical report on the IT index. Further, analysts at Emkay flag that the Nifty IT/Nifty 200 ratio is rebounding from multi-year support held since 2012, pointing to likely sector outperformance. As a trading strategy, the brokerage recommends 31,700–32,900 as the accumulation zone, with a stop loss placed at 30,400 for a likely upside target of 39,000 levels.

data.title: Tata Steel-Apollo deal tests India's reinforced corporate governance rules
data.description:
By Anto Antony and Samie Modak
 
A deal that would hand Tata Steel Ltd. control of a smaller rival triggered a dramatic show of investor anger this week, turning the plan into a test of India’s reinforced corporate governance rules.
 
The basics of the agreement are messy. Tata Steel, a $22 billion piece of the sprawling Tata conglomerate, plans to take a 26.6% share in APL Apollo Tubes Ltd., buying out founder Sanjay Gupta and triggering a mandatory offer for a further 26%. APL Apollo will in turn take Tata’s tubes and color-coated steel business, a deal it will fund initially with debt. Gupta, meanwhile, stays in the business with his family’s SG Tech Engineering agreeing to provide color-coated steel to the new owners.
 
 
For Tata, the purchase is a way of growing in higher-margin corners of the steel market. In the eyes of angry shareholders — who wiped more than $4 billion off the companies’ combined market value over two trading days — it’s a worryingly costly plan, and one that allows Gupta to exit with cash while the remaining APL Apollo investors are left to shoulder an unclear amount of debt, dilution and risk. 
 
The fight is raising questions about India’s ability to enforce minority shareholder protections and ensure that wealth created by tycoons can trickle down.
 
“The real test of India’s corporate governance reforms is whether they can protect minority shareholders when their interests diverge from those of the country’s most powerful business groups,” said Shriram Subramanian, founder and managing director of proxy advisory firm InGovern Research Services.
 
The backlash has already prompted Tata Steel to consider changes to the offer, leaving investors to watch for its next steps.
 
“It would send a clear message that strategic rationale alone is not sufficient to secure shareholder support,” said Akhilesh Kumar, research analyst at Emkay Global Financial Services. “Companies need to ensure that the transaction structure, valuation and funding arrangements are acceptable to all stakeholders, particularly minority shareholders.”
 
A Tata Steel spokesperson said the company was “carefully examining the concerns to determine how best to address them.” Apollo’s Gupta did not immediately respond to Bloomberg queries. 
 
Founding families have been and remain central to India’s economic transformation, building sprawling business empires spanning telecommunications, financial services, energy and infrastructure. Many retain significant control of listed companies even as foreign institutional investors and domestic savers increasingly finance their expansion.
 
Even after a dramatic expansion of India’s stock market over the past decade, founders owned just under 42% of non-state-owned Indian companies at the end of September, while institutional investors held less than 35%, according to corporate information database primeinfobase.com.
 
To counter that weight and to avoid a repeat of major accounting scandals — including the 2009 debacle at Satyam Computer Services Ltd., once one of the country’s largest software exporters — India has tightened oversight and governance rules over the past decade or so.
 
The securities regulator has also strengthened minority shareholders’ powers to block major transactions involving corporate insiders. Rules that took effect in April 2023 extended those safeguards to transactions with unrelated entities if their purpose and effect are to benefit related parties.
 
As a result, there have been notable successes. For example, investors blocked tycoon Anil Agarwal’s 2020 attempt to take Vedanta Ltd. private at what they considered to be a cut-price valuation. Life Insurance Corp. of India, one of the company’s largest public shareholders, said publicly that it would not tender stock below 320 rupees a share — almost four times Vedanta’s indicative price — and investors held out for better terms. The delisting ultimately failed.
 
Earlier this year, rules protecting minority investors allowed shareholders at Linde India Ltd. to reject a proposed transaction with Praxair India, controlled by the same majority owner.
 
Still, there are also incidents where so-called promoters won the day — from some vocal shareholders’ efforts to stop the delisting of ICICI Bank’s brokerage arm last year, to fund manager Invesco’s earlier failure to oust the chief executive of Zee Entertainment.
 
The Tata deal is a test with repercussions at a time when India’s stock market wants to retain domestic and foreign investors eager to bet on its economic growth, even at valuations that sit well above that of other emerging economies.
 
“India’s economic growth alone cannot sustain the valuation premium its companies command in global markets,” said K.G. Suresh, a faculty member at the Indian Institute of Management Bodh Gaya. “Any erosion of investor confidence in corporate governance risks raising the cost of capital for Indian businesses.”
 
The controversy comes at an awkward time for the Tata Group. Its privately held holding company, Tata Sons Pvt., has been embroiled in a months-long dispute over leadership, governance and a regulator-mandated stock market listing.
 
“While the Tata Group is known for its impeccable governance and shareholder friendly conduct, this time around it seems to have been caught in a bind,” said Ankit Agrawal, chief investment officer at Yellowstone Equity, an independent research firm. “It seems Tata Steel got carried away by the hefty valuation being accorded to their color-coated sheets business and the desperation to expand their downstream business.”
 
India’s market watchdog is examining the structure of the transaction, according to people familiar with the matter. A representative of the Securities and Exchange Board of India did not respond to a request for comment.

data.title: HEG Ltd shares list at 25% premium after graphite business demerger
data.description:
HEG Ltd shares, formerly known as HEG Graphite Ltd, made their debut on the bourses on Friday following the demerger of its core graphite electrode business. The stock opened at ₹587 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), a premium of ₹118.75, or 25.36 per cent, over the pre-listing value of ₹468.25.
 
On the BSE, the stock debuted at ₹580, up ₹115.95, or 24.99 per cent, against the pre-listing price of ₹464.05.
 
At listing, the company commanded a market capitalisation of ₹11,192.70 crore, according to BSE data.
 The stock soon hit the lower circuit, falling 5 per cent to ₹551 on the BSE as investors booked profits.
 
 
As per the restructuring, which came into effect in September 2026, the original listed entity (HEG Ltd) was rechristened HEG Advanced Materials Ltd following the demerger. HEG Advanced Materials shares closed 8.4 per cent higher at ₹280.55 on Thursday.
 
HEG Advanced Materials houses the advanced materials, battery energy solutions and green power businesses. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex down 200 pts, Nifty around 25,800; PSU Bank, Metal up 1% each
 
The graphite electrodes business moved into the resulting company, HEG Graphite Ltd, which was later renamed HEG Ltd. It will be a pure-play graphite electrodes company.
 
Notably, the demerger of HEG Ltd was first announced in 2024, and the board later fixed September 7, 2026 as the record date. Under the demerger scheme, HEG Ltd issued shares of the resulting company to eligible shareholders in a 1:1 ratio.
 
Earlier, the company had said that the reorganisation would give each business an independent listing, focused management and the flexibility to pursue its own growth path.
 
As part of the same scheme, Bhilwara Energy Ltd was amalgamated into HEG Advanced Materials Ltd and dissolved without winding up. HEG Advanced Materials Ltd issued eight equity shares of face value ₹2 each to existing shareholders of Bhilwara Energy Ltd for every seven equity shares of face value ₹10 each held in the company.
 
According to a report by Aditya Birla Money, HEG has installed capacity of 100kt, operating at more than 90 per cent utilisation, and generating Ebitda/t of $840 – this equates to ₹7.4 billion of implied Ebitda, which compares with an Ebitda of ₹3.9 billion in FY26. 
 
It noted that the company is expanding capacity by 15kt to 115kt with a planned commissioning in FY29 and capex outlay of ₹6.5 billion. Also,  With an imminent price hike of $$1,000/t though offset partially by increase in raw materials and energy costs, the brokerage believes that HEG Ltd could deliver Ebitda/t of $1,200-1,300/t over FY28-30E.
 
These two drivers (volumes growth and price cycle recovery), could result in Ebitda potentially reaching ₹11-12.5 billion by FY28/29E, nearly doubling from the current implied run-rate of ₹7.4 billion, Aditya Birla Money said in its report.
 
 Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Coal India unit Mahanadi Coalfields lists at 2% discount to IPO price
data.description:
Mahanadi Coalfields IPO listing: Shares of Mahanadi Coalfields made a tepid debut on Dalal Street as they listed at a discount of nearly 2 per cent premium against the initial public offer (IPO) price of ₹136. 
 
The Coal India subsidiary made its NSE debut at ₹134 apiece, down 1.47 per cent. And on BSE, the stock listed 2.10 per cent lower at ₹133.15. 
 
Mahanadi Coalfields is the third Coal India subsidiary to make its debut on the bourses, following Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL) in January 2026 and Central Mine Planning & Design Institute (CMPDIL) in March 2026.
 

Mahanadi Coalfields IPO details

The ₹8,981-crore IPO of Mahanadi Coalfields was available for bidding from November 19 to November 23. The offer received a tepid response as it was booked just 1.52 times at the end of the final day. Overall, it received bids for 74,86,87,390 shares as against 49,30,68,045 shares on offer.  
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex down 200 pts, Nifty around 25,800; SMIDs outperform
 
 
The qualified institutional buyers (QIB) did the heavy lifting as their quota was the only one that sailed through. It was subscribed 4.95 times. Meanwhile, the non-institutional investor (NII) portion was booked just 0.66 times, the retail portion 0.46 times, employee portion at 0.22 times, and the shareholder quota at 0.56 times. 
 
The issue was entirely an offer for sale by promoter Coal India, meaning no proceeds would go to the company. 
 
The price band for Mahanadi Coalfields IPO was set at ₹129 to ₹136 per share. Investors could apply for the offer in lots of 110 shares. The minimum amount of investment required by an individual investor was ₹14,960 based on upper price.
 
Mahanadi Coal is India’s largest single coal producing company by production, engaged in the production of thermal-grade non-coking coal. It also ranks amongst the country’s largest coal resource holders, holding ~9.8 per cent of India’s total coal resource. 
 
Financially, the company has maintained strong profitability despite moderating revenue and earnings. Consolidated revenue from operations declined from INR 31,634.35 crore in FY24 to INR 31,353.02 crore in FY25 and INR 30,549.59 crore in FY26, representing a 1.73% decline CAGR over FY24–26. Consolidated PAT decreased from INR 11,841.55 crores in FY24 to INR 10,825.12 crores in FY25 and INR 10,698.12 crores in FY26.  
ALSO READ: PhonePe warms up for IPO as investor appetite for Indian equities returns
 
Operating cash flow improved to INR 12,477.53 crores in FY26 from INR 7,704.96 crores in FY25, reflecting strong cash generation despite subdued earnings growth. The balance sheet remains highly liquid, with minimal financial borrowings and substantial cash and bank balances, said Ventura. 
 
Key risks, according to the brokerage, include thermal coal demand dependence, pricing and regulatory changes, rising mining costs, environmental obligations and the long-term transition towards renewable energy.

data.title: India Inc margins may fall 50-75 bps, revenue growth at 18-20% in Q3: Icra
data.description:
Rating agency Icra expects revenue growth of Indian companies to moderate to 18-20 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in Q3 FY27, from 24.2 per cent in the previous quarter, as rising input costs and price increases are likely to weigh on volume growth.
 
However, price increases, festive and wedding-season spending, and sustained government capital expenditure are expected to support revenues, even as operating profit margins (OPM) face pressure.
 
In its latest assessment of 3,103 listed companies, excluding those in the financial sector, Icra estimated that aggregate operating margins could decline by 50-75 basis points year-on-year in Q3 FY27, amid higher raw material, fuel, freight and packaging costs.
 
 
The rating agency said the moderation in revenue growth would partly be due to a high base in Q3 FY26, when volumes received a boost following the goods and services tax (GST) rate cuts in September 2025. Companies are also passing on higher raw material, energy, labour and logistics costs to customers through price increases.
 
Icra said inflationary pressures and a possible slowdown in rural demand following El Niño-related crop losses could pose challenges over the next two to three quarters. An uneven monsoon could also weigh on agricultural output, farm incomes and rural consumption.
 
"Icra expects the divergence between domestic-oriented and export-oriented sectors to persist in the near term," said Kinjal Shah, senior vice-president and co-group head, Corporate Ratings, Icra.
 
Sectors such as automobiles, retail, consumer durables and hospitality are likely to perform better, supported by relatively resilient domestic demand. In contrast, export-dependent industries such as information technology and cut and polished diamonds could continue to face challenges amid subdued global demand and macroeconomic uncertainty.
 
A softening of US tariffs could provide some support to apparel and home textile exports, although any fresh tariff-related uncertainty remains a concern, Icra said.
 
On the profitability front, aviation, automobiles, fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), cement and other energy-intensive industries are likely to face margin pressure from higher crude oil prices, palm oil, coal and other key inputs. The resulting increase in freight, packaging and logistics costs is also expected to weigh on profitability.
 
Companies in these sectors have started taking price increases and cost-cutting measures to offset higher expenses arising from the West Asia conflict and the depreciation of the rupee against the US dollar. However, the benefits are expected to come through gradually.
 
Metals and mining companies, upstream oil producers, telecom operators, hospitality players and regulated utilities are relatively better placed, supported by favourable realisations, operating leverage and established mechanisms to pass on higher costs.
 
Despite the expected pressure on margins, corporate credit metrics are likely to remain resilient. Icra expects the interest coverage ratio of its sample companies to stand at 5-5.2 times in Q3 FY27, compared with 5.7 times in Q2 FY27.
 
The ratio is expected to be supported by stable earnings and healthy revenue growth, although higher borrowing costs and lower margins could weigh on it.
 
Icra also cautioned that inflation, product price increases and interest rate hikes could affect consumption, particularly in mass-market and price-sensitive categories. Geopolitical developments, commodity price movements and climate-related risks are also likely to influence business sentiment and private sector capital expenditure plans in the coming quarters.

data.title: IDFC First Bank gains 3% in subdued market; nears 52-week high
data.description:
IDFC First Bank share price movement

 
IDFC First Bank’s share price rose 3 per cent to ₹88.95 on the BSE in Friday’s intraday deals in an otherwise subdued market on expectations of healthy growth over the medium term. 
 
The stock price of the private sector lender quoted close to its 52-week high of ₹89.58 touched on September 23, 2026. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was down 0.2 per cent at 84,158.93 at 09:40 AM. A combined 7.3 million shares changed hands on the NSE and BSE.
 

Jefferies maintains ‘Buy’ rating on IDFC First Bank with TP ₹100

 
Jefferies maintains a ‘Buy’ rating on IDFC First Bank with a target price ₹100 as the brokerage firm believes that with Common Equity Tier 1 (CET-1) at 13 per cent & higher growth, the bank may consider raising capital. Expansion in return on asset (ROA) is key to rerating, the brokerage firm said, and sees 20 per cent compound annual growth rate (CAGR) in loans over FY27-29 and ROA expanding to 1.2 per cent by FY29.
 
 
IDFC First Bank’s management reiterated that the bank can continue to see 20 per cent plus loan growth in the medium-term, aided by network expansion and growth in corporate loans. Growth in deposits should be slightly higher, helping lower loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR). The bank is investing in the current account franchise through lending relationships, tech platforms & services. This can help bring down funding costs and improve corporate lending ROA, analysts at Jefferies said in a report.
 
The Bank’s net interest margins (NIMs) may be stable in near-term and can expand from Q4 aided by rate hikes. Over the medium term, NIMs may moderate as the share of lower-risk loans rises, but a positive jaws effect should open, with operating leverage aiding ROA expansion, the brokerage firm said.
 
IDFC First Bank’s robust deposit growth is expected to sustain, resulting in a higher share of lower-cost deposits in overall funding. Stronger growth in rural, retail & small and medium enterprises (SME) segments will support yields & drive margin expansion. Scale benefits will accrue over the next few years & drive a lower cost-to-income ratio as past investments start to bear fruit, e.g., credit cards. Bank has successful track record of managing retail asset quality across cycles to control credit costs, Jefferies said. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: WhiteOak Capital raises equity exposure to 65%: What it mean for investors
data.description:
WhiteOak Capital Balanced Advantage Fund on Friday said it has increased its net unhedged equity allocation to 64.9% as of October 31, 2026, signalling a more favourable assessment of equity market valuations by the fund’s internal model.
 
The move comes as the market has corrected from its levels at the beginning of the year. But what does a higher equity allocation in a balanced advantage fund mean, how does the valuation-based strategy work, and should investors read it as a signal to invest more in equities?
 
What has changed in WhiteOak’s allocation?
According to the fund house’s update, its proprietary Market Valuation Index declined from 101 in January 2026 to 90 in October. The BSE Sensex, meanwhile, fell from 82,269 to 74,459 over the same period.
 
 
WhiteOak said its model responds to lower valuations by gradually increasing equity exposure. Accordingly, the fund raised its net equity allocation from 61% in January to 64.9% in October.
 
The fund’s positioning has also changed sharply compared with an earlier period of elevated valuations. In September 2024, when the Sensex reached 84,299 and WhiteOak’s valuation index touched 105, the fund maintained a more conservative net equity allocation of 49.6%. WhiteOak Capital Balanced Advantage Fund Raises Net Equity Allocation to 64.9% as Market Valuations Turn Increasingly Attractive.docx
 
What is a balanced advantage fund?
A balanced advantage fund, also known as a dynamic asset allocation fund, is a hybrid mutual fund that invests in both equity and debt. Unlike funds that maintain a relatively fixed allocation, these schemes can increase or reduce their equity and debt exposure based on market conditions and the fund’s investment model. 
 
The idea is to adjust the portfolio across market cycles:
  • When equity valuations appear expensive, the fund may reduce unhedged equity exposure and move more towards debt or hedged positions.
  • When valuations become more attractive, it may increase equity exposure to participate in a potential market recovery.
  • The allocation can change over time, so the fund’s risk profile is not constant.
SEBI’s investor education material describes dynamic asset allocation funds as schemes that can move between equity and debt within a broad range, subject to their investment mandate. 
 
What does “net unhedged equity” mean?
The 64.9% figure refers to the fund’s net unhedged equity exposure — the portion of the portfolio exposed to equity market movements after accounting for hedges.
 
It should not automatically be read as the fund holding exactly 64.9% of its total assets in shares. Balanced advantage funds may also use derivatives to hedge part of their equity exposure. The gross equity allocation, hedged exposure and net equity exposure can therefore be different measures. 
 
For investors, net unhedged equity is an important indicator of how much market risk the fund is taking through its equity positioning at a particular point in time.
 
Does a higher equity allocation mean the market is cheap?
Not necessarily. It means WhiteOak’s internal model currently considers equity valuations more attractive than they were earlier in the year.
 
The fund house’s Market Valuation Index is proprietary, and the release does not provide its full methodology or the precise valuation threshold at which the fund changes its allocation. The index level of 90 should therefore not be treated as a universal measure of whether Indian equities are cheap or expensive.
 
A valuation-based strategy also does not guarantee that a fund will increase equity exposure at the market bottom or reduce it before a correction. Markets can remain expensive or fall further even after valuations have moderated.
 
What should investors make of this?
The increase in equity allocation is a portfolio-positioning update, not a standalone recommendation to invest in the fund.
Balanced advantage funds may be relevant to investors who want a fund to manage the equity-debt mix dynamically rather than make every allocation decision themselves. However, these funds remain market-linked and can incur losses, particularly when their equity exposure is high. 
 
Investors should look beyond the latest allocation and assess the fund’s longer-term performance across market cycles, its investment strategy, expenses, risk level and consistency of execution. They should also consider whether the fund fits their investment horizon and overall asset allocation.
 
Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks. Read all scheme-related documents carefully.

data.title: Delimitation Bill: What it proposes for Lok Sabha and women's quota rollout
data.description:
The Union government has called Parliament to reconvene from November 30 to transact essential government business, amid speculation over the introduction of the proposed Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, linked to delimitation and the implementation of women's reservation.
 
In a post on X on Thursday, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the respective Houses. The Lok Sabha has been requested to meet on Monday, November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will reconvene on Wednesday, December 2. The sittings of both Houses may conclude on December 3.
 
 
The special sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session. Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13 but has not yet been prorogued, which would formally end the session.
 
The government has not disclosed the specific legislative agenda for the three-day sitting. According to news agency PTI, the Union Cabinet is expected to meet on Friday and is likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's reservation proposal.
 

What is delimitation and what do the proposed Bills seek to change?

 
Delimitation is the process of redrawing the boundaries of Lok Sabha and State Assembly constituencies and allocating seats based on changes in population. In India, the exercise is carried out by an independent Delimitation Commission under constitutional provisions, including Articles 81, 82 and 170.
 
Its purpose is to keep the populations of constituencies broadly equal and update the allocation of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
 
The proposed Constitution Amendment Bill seeks to change provisions governing the composition of the House of the People and the allocation of seats among states and Union Territories (UTs). Its key proposals include:
 
Increase in Lok Sabha's maximum strength
 
The Constitution currently provides for a maximum of 550 Lok Sabha members, comprising up to 530 members from states and up to 20 from Union Territories. The Constitution Amendment Bill proposes raising this ceiling to 850 members, with up to 815 members from states and up to 35 from Union Territories.
 
Delimitation based on population
 
The Constitution Amendment Bill proposes reverting to the principle of allocating Lok Sabha seats to states in proportion to their population.
 
Parliament to decide which Census is used
 
The Constitution provides for delimitation after every Census, with the exercise based on population figures from that Census. The Constitution Amendment Bill authorises Parliament to pass a law determining when delimitation will be undertaken and which Census will be used.
 
A separate piece of legislation, the Delimitation Bill, 2026, provides that the latest published Census available on the date the Delimitation Commission is constituted will be used for the exercise. This implies that the 2011 Census would be used for the next delimitation exercise.
 
Setting up of a Delimitation Commission
 
Under the Delimitation Bill, 2026, the Central government may constitute a Delimitation Commission from time to time by notification to readjust and reallocate seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. The Central government will also appoint the commission's chairperson.
 

How could the proposed Bill fast-track women's reservation?

 
The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023, also known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, introduced reservation of one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for women.
 
However, the quota was linked to the first Census conducted after the commencement of the 2023 Act, followed by a delimitation exercise.
 
The proposed 131st Amendment Bill seeks to remove this requirement, allowing the 33 per cent reservation to take effect without waiting for a fresh Census. Instead, it links the implementation of the quota to a delimitation exercise based on the latest published Census figures, which are currently from the 2011 Census.
 
The proposed change is aimed at enabling women's reservation in time for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, rather than delaying its implementation until after the 2027 Census.
 
The Bill proposes changes to Article 334A, which governs the reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies. Under the proposed provision, the reservation would come into force "after an exercise of delimitation is undertaken for this purpose".
 
It further provides that "the seats reserved for women shall be allotted by rotation to different constituencies in a State or Union territory". The reservation would remain in force for 15 years, unless extended by Parliament.
 

What happened when the legislation was previously put to a vote?

 
The proposed legislation failed to secure the required numbers during a special sitting of Parliament on April 17.
 
Of the 528 Lok Sabha members present and voting, 298 voted in favour of the Bill, while 230 opposed it. Under Article 368 of the Constitution, a constitutional amendment requires a special majority of at least two-thirds of members present and voting.
 
This meant the Bill needed 352 votes and fell short by 54.
 
In the current 543-member Lok Sabha, the two-thirds mark would be 362 if all members were present and voting. The ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), which has 320 members, would need support from Opposition parties to secure the required numbers.
 

What is the political arithmetic behind the Bill?

 
The political arithmetic has since changed, with 26 MPs moving out of the Opposition camp.
 
Twenty rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs also joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.
 
Following its alliance with the BJP, the Shiromani Akali Dal's (SAD's) lone Lok Sabha MP is also expected to vote with the government.
 
According to a report by The Hindu, the YSR Congress is reportedly set to extend support to the government on the Bill with its four Lok Sabha MPs.
 

Why could the DMK and NCP (SP) prove crucial to the numbers game?

 
The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight MPs, could play an important role in determining whether the government secures the numbers required to pass the legislation.
 
The DMK has maintained that it would consider supporting the proposed delimitation legislation if Tamil Nadu's existing share of parliamentary representation is protected, irrespective of the increase in the total number of Lok Sabha seats.
 
"If the draft Bill clearly gives us an assurance of protecting our representation in Parliament, we may consider it," a senior MP was quoted as saying by The New Indian Express.
 
The NCP (SP), meanwhile, has indicated that it will decide its position after examining the proposed legislation.
 
According to a Times of India report, party state president Shashikant Shinde said on Thursday that the party would take a call on the delimitation Bill after it was tabled in Parliament and its MPs had examined the provisions. He also played down speculation about differences within the party over the proposed legislation.
 
Separately, according to NDTV, NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule said her party would review the proposed Delimitation Bill once it was formally introduced in Parliament and could support it if its provisions served the national interest.
 

Why is the Congress opposing the proposed delimitation legislation?

 
The Congress has opposed the proposed Delimitation Bill, 2026, with party leaders arguing that it is politically motivated, unilateral and threatens India's federal structure. The party has also criticised the government for calling a special sitting at short notice without Question Hour or Zero Hour.
 
Congress leader Jairam Ramesh alleged that the gap since August had been used for "Operation Lotus" to gather the numbers needed to pass the legislation.

data.title: China industrial profit growth hits 5-month high as recovery remains uneven
data.description:
Profit growth at China's industrial firms accelerated in October to the fastest in five months, supported by improving conditions in parts of the manufacturing sector, although broader economic momentum remained subdued.
 
The industrial profits data are closely watched as a gauge of corporate health, investment appetite and the effectiveness of Beijing's stimulus measures. The figures also offer clues on whether stronger earnings could reduce pressure for further policy easing.
 
Profits at industrial ‌firms rose 20.1% from a year earlier last month, versus  a 14.4% gain in September, data from  the National Bureau of Statistics showed on Friday. Profits were up 16% in the first 10 months, accelerating from a  15.5% increase in the January-September period.
 
 
But the breakdown highlighted a widening divergence across sectors.
 
Profit growth in AI-related industries and upstream sectors is outpacing that of downstream industries, while external demand remains an important source of support, said Ding Meng, CITIC Bank International's chief China economist.
 
The bureau's data showed that profits in computer, telecommunications and other electronic equipment manufacturing doubled in the first 10 months,  while furniture manufacturing posted a decline of 52.4%.
 
"The recovery remains uneven and provides a more mixed signal on the health of the broader ‌economy," said Lynn Song, ING's Greater China chief economist.
 
Broader Chinese indices were muted while tech stocks rebounded strongly. The  CSI Semiconductor Industry Index jumped more than 5%, while the Hang Seng Tech Index was up 3%.
 
The disparity underscores the challenges facing policymakers as domestic demand remains weak and continues to weigh on large parts of the corporate sector. Many manufacturers have increasingly relied on overseas sales ‌to sustain growth, leaving them exposed to rising trade  frictions and geopolitical risks.
 
Beijing has rolled out a ‌series of support measures in recent months, including interest-rate cuts, liquidity injections and targeted financing support for sectors such as technology, ‌manufacturing and infrastructure.
 
Still, analysts say the impact has been mixed, with weak household demand and lingering strains in the property  sector continuing to drag on the broader recovery.
 
"The robust pace of profit growth further reinforces expectations that there will be no additional monetary policy easing in the near term," Ding said.
 
The outlook  for exports, a key source of support for manufacturers this year, has also become less certain. Concern over potential tariff increases and other trade restrictions, particularly in the United States and the European Union, has raised ‌questions about the sustainability of export-driven growth.
 
Looking ahead, a potential slowdown in AI data centre investment, concerns over AI-sector profitability and ‌leverage, and the risk of further Western restrictions on Chinese exports mean that "boosting domestic demand as soon as possible remains the key to sustaining profit growth," Ding said.
 
Industrial profit figures cover firms with annual revenue of at least 20 million yuan ($3 million) from main operations.
